answers: Come down and sit in the dust

easy.explanation: The Lord says that Babylon’s nakedness will be uncovered and her shame will be seen.
easy.q: What will be exposed in Babylon?

answers: From a lady to a humiliated captive
medium.explanation: Babylon loses her royal position and is brought down into humiliation.
medium.q: What change in Babylon's status is described in these verses?

medium.q: In the KJV, what does “make bare the leg” mean?

answers: It adds to the difficult and humiliating labor Babylon must undertake

paragraphs.title: Babylon's Loss of Status and Responsibility

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness.”
easy.q: How is Babylon commanded to sit?

easy.explanation: Babylon will no longer be called “The lady of kingdoms.”
easy.q: What will Babylon no longer be called?

answers: Without mercy and with a heavy yoke
easy.explanation: Babylon showed the people no mercy and laid a very heavy yoke upon them.
easy.q: How did Babylon treat the people placed in her hand?

answers: Because she did not know they were Israelites
medium.explanation: Although the Lord gave Israel into Babylon’s hand, Babylon showed them no mercy.
medium.q: Why was Babylon responsible even though the Lord gave Israel into her hand?

answers: A burden or form of bondage
medium.explanation: A yoke represents a burden or bondage placed upon someone.
medium.q: What does “yoke” mean in “thou hast very heavily laid thy yoke”?

answers: Her cruelty is presented as part of her guilt before judgment
Her cruelty guarantees her lasting rule
medium.explanation: The passage recalls Babylon’s cruelty before describing her confidence and coming downfall.
medium.q: How are Babylon's loss of status and her treatment of Israel connected?

answers: Babylon's loss of honor and public prominence
challenge.explanation: Silence and darkness contrast with Babylon’s former position as the lady of kingdoms.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness” emphasize?

answers: She acted within a situation the Lord allowed, but was still judged for her actions
She was stronger than the Lord
She received no authority at all
challenge.explanation: The Lord gave Israel into her hand, but Babylon remained accountable for showing no mercy.

answers: She assumed that her rule would last forever
She gave up her power immediately

easy.q: How is Babylon described at the beginning of this section?

easy.q: What did Babylon say she would not know?

easy.explanation: The passage says that desolation shall come upon Babylon suddenly.
easy.q: What will come upon Babylon suddenly?

answers: She trusted in her own power, wisdom, and position
medium.explanation: Babylon trusted in her wickedness, wisdom, knowledge, and supposed uniqueness.
medium.q: What caused Babylon to feel secure?

Babylon will discover a way to escape

paragraphs.title: Sorcery, Astrologers, and the Absence of Salvation

easy.explanation: The prophet challenges Babylon to stand with her enchantments, sorceries, and counselors.
easy.q: What is Babylon challenged to rely upon?

answers: They will fail and be unable to deliver themselves
easy.explanation: The astrologers and counselors will not be able to save Babylon or even themselves from the flame.
easy.q: What will happen to those who tried to save Babylon?

answers: Wander every one to his quarter
easy.explanation: The merchants will scatter, wandering each to his own quarter, and none will save Babylon.
easy.q: What will Babylon's merchants do at the end of the passage?

answers: To mock Babylon and test whether her occult practices can save her
To invite Babylon to a celebration
To guarantee the success of her sorceries
medium.explanation: The challenge is ironic because Babylon’s enchantments will prove powerless.
medium.q: What is the purpose of the challenge, “Stand now with thine enchantments”?

answers: People who claim to interpret the stars and predict events
medium.explanation: These terms refer to people who use heavenly signs in an attempt to predict the future.
medium.q: What are “the astrologers, the stargazers, and the monthly prognosticators”?

answers: All of her sources of confidence prove powerless
They leave her after her victory
medium.explanation: The passage shows that neither occult wisdom nor commercial connections can deliver Babylon.
medium.q: Why can neither the counselors nor the merchants save Babylon?

answers: Babylon's helpers are weak and quickly consumed
They become a source of warmth and protection
They build a wall around Babylon
challenge.explanation: Stubble burns easily, illustrating the weakness and helplessness of Babylon’s supporters.
challenge.q: What does the comparison “they shall be as stubble” mean?

answers: Babylon's supposed sources of help provide no comfort or refuge
Babylon finds a safe place to warm herself
The merchants provide her with light
